assertions.subject: Intestinal obstruction
assertions.quote: Increased intestinal contractility, which occurs proximally and distal to the obstruction, is a characteristic response.

assertions.subject: Intestinal obstruction
assertions.quote: Subsequently, intestinal peristalsis slows as the intestine or stomach proximal to the point of obstruction dilates and fills with gastrointestinal secretions and swallowed air.

assertions.subject: Intestinal obstruction
assertions.quote: Intraluminal dilation also increases intraluminal pressure.

assertions.subject: Intestinal obstruction
assertions.quote: Edema ensues, and the bowel wall proximal to the site of blockage may become hypoxemic.

assertions.subject: Intestinal obstruction
assertions.quote: Epithelial necrosis can be identified within 12 h of obstruction.

assertions.subject: Intestinal obstruction
assertions.quote: Ultimately, arterial blood supply may become so compromised that full-thickness ischemia, necrosis, and perforation result.

assertions.subject: Intestinal obstruction
assertions.quote: Stasis increases the bacteria counts within the jejunum and ileum.

assertions.subject: Ogilvie’s syndrome
assertions.quote: Some patients with Ogilvie’s syndrome have colonic dysmotility due to abnormalities of their autonomic nervous system that may be inherited.
